History: Syrophoenicia was the Phoenician coast as part of the Roman province of Syria. A Syrophoenician woman sought Jesus for her demon-possessed daughter, and he praised her faith; Mark names her people explicitly, 'a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation.'
Culture: Phoenician cities, Greek-speaking under Roman Syria.
Religion: Pagan background; the woman's persistence and faith are the story's point.
BibleConnection: Mark is the only Gospel to name this people, and he does so precisely to mark the woman as an outsider to Israel whose faith Jesus honoured.
